title: ADB to help plan 1,000 MW of solar and storage; new strategy in talks
excerpt: ADB will advise on six solar and battery projects worth more than $1 billion in private money, and is consulting on its 2028 to 2032 country strategy.

image.alt: Aerial view of a large solar power plant among fields in Bangladesh

content:
The Asian Development Bank (ADB) signed an agreement on Tuesday (17 November) to give transaction advice to five more solar and battery storage projects in Bangladesh, bdnews24.com's Bangla edition reported. This brings its support to six projects with a combined capacity of more than 1,000 MW, ADB said. The projects aim to draw in more than $1 billion of private investment.

The first is the 130 MW Sonagazi solar project in Feni, which will have 26 megawatt-hours of battery storage. Its tender is expected within 2026. ADB will also help Invest Bangladesh and the Bangladesh Power Development Board (BPDB) check whether government land is suitable for the five new projects. The agreement was signed by Mostafa Kamal of Invest Bangladesh's PPP Division, BPDB Secretary Afroza Sultana and ADB Country Director Qingfeng Zhang, bdnews24.com's Bangla edition reported.

"Bangladesh has an opportunity to build a more secure, sustainable, and investment-ready energy future," Zhang said.

A new country strategy

The deal came during a visit from 16 to 18 November by a delegation led by Sona Shrestha, ADB's Director General for South Asia. With Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury, the delegation launched "PPP Monitor: Bangladesh", which tracks more than 500 indicators. Views gathered during the visit will feed ADB's country partnership strategy for 2028 to 2032, The Business Standard reported.

Why it matters

The projects support the government's targets of at least 20% of electricity from renewables by 2030 and 30% by 2040. Large solar farms need a lot of land, so climate, land rights and farmers' groups will want to see how sites are chosen. The next ADB country strategy will also shape one of Bangladesh's biggest sources of development finance for years, and civil society can take part in the consultations.

What to watch

The Sonagazi tender, which government land is offered for the other five projects, and how ADB consults civil society on the new strategy.
